intro: Retail sales builds persuasion, service and negotiation skills that many customer-facing jobs need. Of the 25 careers below, the closest fit is door-to-door and street sales, with a 90% match and a BLS May 2025 median of $41,380, or 17% more than the $35,410 retail salespersons earn.
why_it_works: On the sales floor you read what a shopper wants, explain a product quickly and close without pushing. O*NET rates persuasion at 3.88 out of 5 for this job, and the same mix of selling and service runs through customer service, promoter and sales representative roles. Almost every match needs no extra schooling. The skills to add are more technical: systems analysis, operations analysis and some programming for sales software.
tips: Turn store numbers into resume lines: average sale, add-on rate or customer ratings are results an employer can check.
Look at business-to-business sales, where Sales Representatives of Services earn a median of $69,990, or 98% more than retail pay.
Ask about a shift-lead role first: First-Line Supervisors of Retail Sales Workers earn $48,520, which is 37% more.

faq.q: What jobs can former retail salespersons do?
faq.a: The closest matches by skills are door-to-door and street sales (90%), Demonstrators and Product Promoters (88%) and Telemarketers (86%), based on O*NET 31.0. Customer Service Representatives are also close at 83%, with a median of $44,770, which is 26% more than the $35,410 retail median.

faq.q: Which careers for former retail salespersons pay more?
faq.a: 18 of the 25 matches pay more than the $35,410 retail median. The largest gains are Gambling Managers at $93,220 (163% more), sales representatives of services at $69,990 (98% more) and Advertising Sales Agents at $64,820 (83% more), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do retail salespersons need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: Usually not. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than retail salespersons already have, including all of the top 10. Training is mostly on the job; in street and door-to-door sales, 57% of workers have less than a high school diploma.

faq.q: What skills should retail salespersons learn next?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work across the closest matches are systems analysis, systems evaluation, operations analysis and programming. Your people skills are already strong: O*NET rates service orientation at 3.75 and social perceptiveness at 3.5 out of 5 for retail sales, so the gap is mostly technical.
